summary: Intermittent p99 latency and timeouts for identical conversational turns due to KV prefetch starvation on hot keys
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent high p99 latency and occasional 504 timeouts for identical conversational turns (repeat prompts) after short idle windows. Problem affects a subset of sessions that are 'hot' (high QPS on the same conversation id) and reproduces against the customer's dedicated capacity pool in us-east.

Impact:
- Multiple user-facing requests for NarrativeAI saw p99 generator latency climb from ~120ms to >2.5s, with some requests eventually 504ing.
- Customer reports degraded product experience for follow-up messages (idempotent repeated prompts) and increased error rates.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated (customer-dedicated GPU pool) in us-east
- Production traffic from NarrativeAI (dedicated tier)
- Affected models: redwood-rlhf-13b (primary), fallback to open-llama-13b observed

Steps to reproduce (from customer):
1) Start a conversational session and send an initial prompt that warms model and KV cache.
2) Send 3–6 identical follow-up turns spaced at ~200–500ms intervals.
3) Wait ~6–12 seconds idle.
4) Send the same follow-up turn again (identical tokens).
5) Observe p99 spike or 504 on the repeated turn in ~5–15% of sessions.

Observed behavior:
- The first repeated turns after a short idle often hit cold-path prefetching and trigger a small fan-out to KV shards, but when the same hot key is continuously requested the prefetch logic sometimes defers re-population, causing serialized misses across replicas and amplified latency.
- Logs show prefix lookup misses followed by sequential backoff/retry patterns. KV lease/lease-stale timings align with observed 6–12s window.

Expected behavior:
- Identical conversational turns should hit prefix/KV fast-path and return sub-200ms response in dedicated env.

Attachments / links:
- Support logs (redacted) attached by customer: s3://support-uploads/narrativeai/2026-03-09/payloads.zip
- APM traces linked in Confluence runbook

investigation_notes: Metric correlation: prefix_lookup_miss and kvcache.backfill_queue_length spike aligned with p99 latency window.

Observed lease ttl mismatch: leases expire at ~8s, but prefetch re-enqueue uses a conservatively large backoff with a 10s floor for keys previously seen as 'hot', which allows a small window where client requests trigger serialized cache repopulation.

Hot-key fanout: single conversation id caused many in-flight requests; scheduler currently favors fairness across keys > this leads to repeated de-prioritization of the same key's prefetch in favor of new keys, causing reserialized cold-paths.
Reproduction harness: Customer provided a harness which simulates 50 sessions with repeated identical turns at 200–500ms spacing; reproduced p99 spikes locally using dedicated-sim mode.

Potential risk of aggressive prefetch: increasing prefetch aggressiveness could increase KV read QPS and burst costs; must ensure no impact on latency for other keys/tenants in shared path (but this is dedicated pool for customer).
Relevant linked tickets: SUP-34121 (cache-coherence window), SUP-78320 (session cache coherence delay) — similar symptoms but different root cause related to prefetch scheduling.
next_steps: 1) Ship and smoke-test runtime patch to reduce prefetch backoff floor for hot keys (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4129).
2) Deploy to NarrativeAI's dedicated pool during low-traffic window and monitor p99, KV read QPS, CPU/GPU utilization for 24h.
3) If stable, roll change into general dedicated-config with feature flag and add automated canary thresholds to detect KV QPS regressions.
4) Update kvcache runbook and create a telemetry dashboard showing prefetch re-enqueue counts, lease expirations, and hot-key contention alerts.
5) Follow up with customer for acceptance test and schedule post-mortem draft if needed.
resolution: Partial mitigation applied: temporary config change reduced prefetch backoff threshold for NarrativeAI's pool and produced immediate p99 improvement. A runtime patch (PR #4129) has been drafted to more robustly handle hot-key re-enqueue behavior and will be canaried to the customer's dedicated pool. Monitoring is in place; awaiting 24–48h stable signal before promoting to broader rollout. Documenting follow-up items in Confluence.
workaround: Reduced kvcache.prefetch_hotkey_threshold for the customer's dedicated pool to force earlier repopulation of hot-key prefixes. Customer observed lower p99 during testing. If recurrence happens, advise temporary traffic shaping to reduce hot-key QPS.
